Hi, I'm Lena. I have worked with design awards for ten years, and I have seen thousands of entries. People think the jury studies every project for an hour. That's not true. The first time, a jury member often looks at an entry for about one minute. So the best entries show the problem first, in one or two sentences, and then the solution. The most common mistake? I have seen it many times: entries with too much text and no clear story. My advice is simple. Imagine you are telling the story to a friend from another country. If your friend understands it, the jury will understand it too.

I've been to the ceremony in Berlin twice: the first time as a guest, and the second time as a winner. And the second time was very different. Before the show, the staff told us where to sit and what to do. When it was our turn, we waited at the side of the stage, and when they called our name, we walked up. It was only thirty seconds, but my legs were shaking. After the ceremony, there was a party, and that's when the real fun started. I have never met so many designers from so many countries in one night. My advice? Bring business cards, and talk to people. Everybody is happy, and everybody wants to talk.
